## Analysis

**Test image key features:**
- Corn kernels photographed under UV/blacklight illumination
- Several kernels exhibit bright teal/cyan-green fluorescence
- This is the classic **aflatoxin fluorescence test** — Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxins B1/B2 that fluoresce bright blue-green under long-wave UV light
- Standard diagnostic method used specifically to detect Aspergillus contamination

**Ruling out other classes:**
- All other ear rots (Diplodia = white mold, Gibberella = pink/red, Trichoderma = dark green, Fusarium = salmon/pink starburst) do not produce this UV fluorescence pattern
- Leaf diseases (rust, gray leaf spot, NCLB, etc.) are entirely inconsistent — wrong plant part and no UV imagery
- The bright teal fluorescence is essentially pathognomonic for Aspergillus aflatoxin contamination

The Aspergillus reference collage confirms olive-green to gray-green powdery mold on kernels (visible in normal light), and this UV image is a different diagnostic representation of the same disease — specifically the aflatoxin screening test.
